result.title: FlowGenesis: Representation-Driven Self-Organization of Neural Architectures
result.summary: Deep neural networks typically rely on architectures specified before training, despite the continuous evolution of their internal representations. We introduce FlowGenesis, a framework in which neural architectures adapt through neuron birth and pruning guided by Representation Flux, a local statistic capturing changes in minibatch mean activations. Neurons exhibiting persistently high Flux undergo splitting designed to approximately preserve the network function, while neurons with low Flux and low activity are pruned. This mechanism allows network capacity to evolve without prescribing a target architecture or performing a separate architecture search. Experiments on image and text classi- fication show that networks initialized with different sizes approach similar final neuron-count ranges within each dataset while maintaining comparable predictive performance. We further extend FlowGenesis to continual learning, where representation-guided structural adaptation reduces the neurons and parameters allocated to successive tasks while maintaining accuracy comparable to fixed-width Progressive Neural Networks in a task-incremental learning setting. These findings demonstrate that neural architectures can adapt through feedback between representation learning and structural change, suggesting an alternative to prescribing network capacity before training.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 FlowGenesis 框架，依据「Representation Flux」这一刻画 minibatch 平均激活变化的局部统计量，在训练中分裂高 Flux 神经元并剪除低 Flux、低活跃神经元，使网络容量自我演化；在图像与文本分类及持续学习中验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 用内部表示变化统计驱动结构增减的思路，或可为动态计算分配、状态更新与容量自适应提供可核查线索，但论文未涉及多模态推理或推理期 latent 状态。
